Do the numbers agree? A data audit of the 2025-26 Atlantic 10 season

Ian Kachadorian

The question. Every game produces three records of the same events: the play-by-play log, the team box score and the player box score. If the data is right, all three agree. I pulled the public ESPN data for every game an Atlantic 10 team played in 2025-26 (335 games, 157,377 play-by-play events) and counted each one against the others, the same way a stock count is reconciled against the ledger.

The answer. The data is good but not clean. Of 115,846 comparisons, 660 disagree, and 165 of 335 games reconcile completely. Scoring is exact: points, made threes and made free throws match in every team-game. The errors sit in the judgment stats, and one stat, assists, accounts for 51% of them.

What I found

  1. Assists are the weak point. Play-by-play assists match the team box score in only 79.1% of team-games; every other stat matches in 97.3% or more. The play-by-play is short by a net 173 assists over the season.

  2. The gap is uneven across arenas, but it is not a fixed arena habit. In games hosted by St. Bonaventure, 47% of team-games have an assist mismatch; in games hosted by Rhode Island, it is 3%. My first read was that each arena’s scoring crew enters assists differently. I tested that against 2024-25 and it did not hold (see “Does it repeat?” below).

  3. It changes a ranking. By the box score, St. Bonaventure was 2nd in the conference in assists per game (15.7). Counted from play-by-play, they drop to 4th (15.0). Any lineup or on/off assist number built from play-by-play carries that error.

  4. One game holds 13% of all mismatches. St. Bonaventure 83, Ohio 88 (2025-12-13) has 83 on its own: missing three-point attempts, turnovers, steals and fouls for both teams, which looks like a stretch of the game missing from the feed.

  5. The obvious sort key is wrong. Sorting events by sequence_number puts them out of game order in 284 of 335 games (918 places where the clock runs backward). Sorting by game_play_number is correct in every game. Anyone computing lineups or runs from the wrong column gets wrong answers without an error message.

Does it repeat? A second season

I ran the same checks on 2024-25 to see whether the same arenas had the same assist gaps. They did not.

  • No carry-over. Across the 14 arenas in both seasons, the rank correlation between one year’s mismatch rate and the next is -0.07, which is no relationship. St. Bonaventure’s home games went from 8% mismatched to 47%.
  • The whole conference got worse. The share of team-games with an assist mismatch rose from 10.4% to 19.9%.
  • I do not know why. The feed changed in 2025-26: 182 of 335 games use new play-by-play wording that appears in no 2024-25 game. But within 2025-26, games with the new wording are no worse than the rest (20% against 22%), so the wording change does not explain it.
  • The older season has different problems. In 2024-25, 58 of 355 games have play-by-play that does not account for every point, 6 of them with no play-by-play at all. Offensive rebounds match the box score in only 56% of team-games, because the play-by-play logs 789 more than the box score does, consistent with dead-ball team rebounds being coded as offensive rebounds that season.

The practical point: the errors are not stable from year to year, so a one-time cleanup does not last. The checks have to run on every game.

The checks

Check Comparisons Mismatches Match rate Games affected
Box score arithmetic 2,010 1 99.95% 1
Play-by-play vs player box 95,746 422 99.56% 152
Play-by-play vs team box 9,380 210 97.76% 137
Player box sum vs team box 8,040 26 99.68% 25
Player minutes vs game length 670 1 99.85% 1
  • Play-by-play vs team box: 14 stats per team per game, counted from events and compared with the official team line.
  • Play-by-play vs player box: the same stats for each player.
  • Player box sum vs team box: the player lines must add up to the team line.
  • Player minutes vs game length: 200 team minutes, plus 25 for each overtime.
  • Box score arithmetic: points equal twos, threes and free throws; total rebounds equal offensive plus defensive; each team’s opponent score equals the opponent’s own score.

Limits

This is public ESPN data loaded with the hoopR package, not CBB Analytics’ own feed, so the specific errors may differ from yours. The scores in this play-by-play were rebuilt by hoopR, so the running score cannot be tested independently. A mismatch shows that two records disagree; it does not show which one is right. That takes film or the official scorer’s report.

The method carries over to any feed. Every mismatch is listed by game, team and player in output/2026/discrepancies.csv (and output/2025/ for the earlier season) and in the app (app.R).
